spec_match.rationale: column-rule in the 1rem column gaps is correct usage, but the grid declares `gap: 0 1rem`, so there is no row gap for row-rule to draw in — the page's 'row rules separate the rows' claim cannot render even in a supporting browser, as its own code comment ('implied 0 gap here') half-admits.

interactive.rationale: Column/row toggles, style select, width slider and colour picker all drive custom properties on the live grid and regenerate the CSS output (assessed from code review and the rendered DOM; the controls were not driven in this session).

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises toggles, live style adjustment and the old-boilerplate comparison — all present.

edge_cases.rationale: A static note honestly says rules don't render in older browsers, but there is no live detection, so in this browser the toggles appear to do nothing with only that note as a hint; the zero-row-gap case is unexamined.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5157805733183488 and the Chrome Developers gap-decorations blog.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite covers the real surface and honestly fails 6 of 8 in this browser.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Cloud-fallback observation only, NOT browser-verified per auto-research.md §0 — headless Chromium 141 (full-page screenshot + DOM, not chrome-devtools-mcp): table, controls and generated CSS render cleanly; rule rendering is unsupported here and the toggles/selects were not driven. chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud session (the auto-research.md section-0 blocker applies, so this is NOT browser verification): what was exercised is page load, full-page screenshot read, served/dumped DOM state and the /conformance/ route result; driving every control and capturing console/network evidence remains for an MCP-equipped session.

design_system.rationale: Variables throughout; .rule-toggle.active sets background and color together; positive/negative cell colours are accent variables.

accessibility.rationale: Controls are native with aria-labels, but the 'data table' is a div grid with no table/row/columnheader roles, the width slider has no visible value readout, and the regenerated CSS output is not announced.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Controls wrap and the table caps at 700px; clean at 1280px headless, but five columns of monospace currency at ≈360px likely pinch or clip (untested here).

openQuestions.title: Give the table a real row gap so row-rule can actually draw
openQuestions.detail: With `gap: 0 1rem` the row gap is zero, so the row-rule the page sells ('row rules separate the rows') has no gap to render in even on Chrome 149+ — the visible row separation comes from header/total borders. Set a small row gap (e.g. gap: 2px 1rem, or expose a row-gap slider) and re-verify in a supporting browser that toggling row-rule visibly changes the rows.

openQuestions.title: Detect missing support live instead of relying on the static note
openQuestions.detail: In this pre-support browser every control appears inert. Probe CSS.supports('row-rule-color','red') and swap the note to an active 'your browser does not render gap rules — showing border fallback' state (optionally applying the border fallback the note describes) so the demo is honest and still instructive.

openQuestions.title: Give the revenue table real table semantics
openQuestions.detail: The grid of divs reads as unstructured text to assistive tech. Add role=table/row/columnheader/cell (or restructure as <table> with display:grid on a wrapper) so the 'data table' concept is actually a data table non-visually.

openQuestions.title: Show the slider value and announce CSS output changes
openQuestions.detail: The width range has no textual readout, and #css-output updates silently; add a value label and aria-live=polite (or a copy button) for the generated CSS.

openQuestions.title: Clarify that one colour input drives both axes
openQuestions.detail: The single picker (aria-label 'Col color') sets both column and row rule colours; either label it 'rule colour' or split it into two pickers to match the per-axis framing of the rest of the UI.

summary: Reviewed with the headless-Chromium-141 cloud fallback (not chrome-devtools-mcp): full-page screenshot + DOM of /v149/css-gap-decorations/data-table-rules/ and the feature /conformance/ route (HTTP 200; panel 2 pass / 6 fail / 0 blocked). A genuinely interactive and well-referenced page, but its row-rule half is structurally unable to render because the grid's row gap is zero, support detection is a static sentence rather than a live state, and the div-based table has no table semantics. Controls were not driven headless.
